dedupe_keys.name: pedestrian tsunami evacuation times for three california probabilistic tsunami hazard zones

description: This USGS data release gives pedestrian travel times out of tsunami hazard zones along the California coast, for evacuation areas matching 475-year, 975-year and 2,475-year average return periods from probabilistic tsunami hazard analysis, at four walking speeds. It was published on ScienceBase on 12 August 2020 by Jeff Peters, Jason Sherba, Kevin Henry and Nathan Wood of the USGS with Rick Wilson, supporting the article 'Variations in community evacuation potential related to average return periods in probabilistic tsunami hazard analysis'. Files are travel-time shapefiles for each zone and speed and tables of impaired-walk travel times for all zones by parcel land use and flow depth class. Coverage: California coastal communities; the study found that the choice of return period substantially changed the number of tax-lot parcels in evacuation areas but not their primary land use. Access: ScienceBase (142 MB shapefiles, 1.9 MB tables). Licence: not stated in the metadata read; free. Caveats: results depend on the four walking speeds modelled. Simulation uses: tsunami evacuation planning, siting vertical evacuation refuges and comparing hazard zones for land-use policy. Related records: the Kutupalong evacuation and UFRGS evacuation drill records.
